newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Czech gas deal opens door to east Europe.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Czech gas deal opens door to east Europe.

text.p: Norway's preliminary agreement to supply the Czech Republic with gas, its first with an eastern European consumer, proved the Scandinavian producer can compete as a supplier to the region, Norway's minister of industry and energy Jens Stoltenberg said on Wednesday.

Under the agreement with Czech state natural gas importer Transgas AS, Norway hopes to transport initial supplies of gas from the start of next year, growing to three billion cubic meters a year for a 20 year period from 2002.

"Although volumes are small compared to total Norwegian volumes in Europe, this shows we are in a position to supply gas to the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe," Stoltenberg told delegates at an oil and gas conference in Stavanger.

Norwegian gas exports to Europe are set to reach 60 billion cubic meters a year early in the next century, but the eastern European gas market has traditionally been the exclusive domain of Russian gas giant Gazprom.
The Czech Republic currently uses just over nine bcm a year but consumption is expected to rise to 12-13 bcm by the turn of the century.
Czech government officials have said they want to diversify supplies away from Moscow.
Transgas said on Tuesday that pipeline arrangements had to be finalised before a full agreement with Norway was completed.
Stoltenberg said the gas supplies would mainly substitute the use of coal in Czech households and the small industrial sector, but could eventually be used for power generation.
